The full trace is now clear. I am ready to present the exact delivery function, source path, and protection mechanism.

Configuration and validation live in `user_service_webhooks.go` (`CreateUserWebhook`, `UpdateUserWebhook`, `ValidateURL`). Dispatch logic sits in `memo_service_webhooks.go` (`DispatchMemo*Webhook`), which loads webhooks and calls `webhook.PostAsync(payload)`. That method enqueues the payload to `asyncPostQueue` in `webhook.go` (lines 184–196). Worker goroutines in `init()` (lines 42–55) consume the queue and execute the actual HTTP request through `Post()`.

`Post()` in `webhook.go` (lines 119–180) executes the HTTP request via `safeClient.Do(req)` at line 152. Config-time validation lives in `validate.go` (lines 62–83), where `ValidateURL` performs a DNS lookup and rejects reserved CIDRs using `isReservedIP`. Runtime protection is provided by a custom `Transport.DialContext` (`safeDialContext`) in `webhook.go` (lines 32–36, 59–77). This re-resolves the hostname at dial time and blocks reserved IPs, preventing DNS rebinding.

`isReservedIP` in `validate.go` (lines 44–54) blocks `reservedCIDRs` including 127.0.0.0/8, RFC1918 ranges, link-local, and IPv6 equivalents. The `--allow-private-webhooks` flag in `main.go` (line 49) can disable this check.
